# MicroDuck Sports Policy and Task Development Topic Team Learning Recruitment

## Recruitment Text

Can a 25 cm long open-source duckling learn through reinforcement learning to walk steadily, maintain balance on a sphere, move forward on a stilt, or achieve real physical contact with a pendulum and a ladder?

We plan to conduct a series of specialized courses around MicroDuck, covering robot models, MuJoCo simulation, reinforcement learning policies, and edge-based inference. Everyone will read the code together, run the notebooks, reproduction existing policies, compare with local experiments, and analyze the reasons for failures, before integrating these policies into the BPU inference chain of the Sweet Potato RDK X5.

> Replay description: GPU video display workstation for policy reasoning, BPU video recording for RDK X5 policy reasoning and Ubuntu physical simulation. Running the BPU unit of the Notebook again generates a new closed loop video. The ladder includes community ladder climbing demonstrations and local handrail contact phase experiments; browser perturbation demonstrations involve external force applied by the mouse.

## What to Learn Together

- Read the MJCF, joint and actuator configurations to understand how observation and action dimensions correspond to the robot;
- Understand PPO, SAC/FastSAC, Actor-Critic, reward functions, and curriculum learning;
- Observe contact dynamics in MuJoCo, learn training, replay, success rate evaluation, and failure analysis;
- Start with existing checkpoints or controllable small-scale training, and gradually develop a task-specific policy;
- Learn ONNX export, X5 HBM compilation, and RDK X5 BPU inference closed loop.

The Notebook is organized by task. Walking/navigation directly falls under existing policies; physical disturbances are used for observing simulation interactions; basketball, stilts, swinging, and ball balance each retain training or continuous training entry points; the ladder surface Notebook is used for contact task experiments and policy deployment learning, with community-level climbing strategy videos serving as action references. Each Notebook stores a snapshot of the results of executed units, and training steps are carried out based on switches, checkpoints, and device conditions within the Notebook.

## RDK X5 Practice

It is planned to use the RDK X5 BPU as the policy inference endpoint: the workstation performs physical simulation and rendering, while RDK infers and returns actions during the control cycle. Training will still be conducted on the workstation/GPU, and ONNX must be compiled into HBM using the corresponding toolchain. The special project focuses on practical side-side implementation for the sweet potato RDK X5; joint activities, device support, and cooperation identities shall be based on the officially confirmed information between both parties.

## Who is suitable for

- Interested in robot motion control, reinforcement learning, or simulation, and willing to start with runnable examples;
- Familiar with basic Python, and willing to collaborate on troubleshooting environment issues, model interfaces, and simulation failures;
- Looking to participate in any aspect of policy training, model deployment, evaluation design, or tutorial creation.

There is no physical MicroDuck, but RDK X5 can also start learning code and simulation first. Formal training requires Linux/Ubuntu and a suitable GPU; without a GPU, you can begin with reading, model inspection, existing policy replays, and small smoke verifications.
